reading_md:
## Why this unit matters for a Vice Principal

A Vice Principal in a Delhi government school is the officer who signs admission registers, handles complaints of corporal punishment, receives a POCSO disclosure from a class teacher, arranges a scribe for a child with disability, and chairs School Management Committee (SMC) meetings. UPSC therefore asks the **operational** parts of four laws: the **RTE Act 2009**, **POCSO Act 2012**, **RPwD Act 2016** and **JJ Act 2015**. Most questions turn on an age, a number, a section or a date. Learn those exactly.

## Constitutional base

| Provision | Content | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Art 21A** | Free and compulsory education for children **6–14** "in such manner as the State may by law determine" | Inserted by the **86th Amendment Act 2002**; in force **1 April 2010** with the RTE Act |
| **Art 45** (substituted) | State to provide early childhood care and education (ECCE) until age **6** | Directive Principle, not enforceable |
| **Art 51A(k)** | Parent or guardian to provide education opportunities to child/ward aged 6–14 | **11th Fundamental Duty** |
| Art 24 | No child below 14 in factory, mine or hazardous employment | Fundamental Right |
| Art 39(e), (f) | Protect children from abuse; childhood protected against exploitation | DPSP |
| Art 46 | Educational interests of weaker sections, SC/ST | DPSP |

Key cases: *Mohini Jain* (1992) and *Unni Krishnan* (1993) read education into Art 21. *Society for Unaided Private Schools of Rajasthan* (2012) upheld the RTE Act but exempted unaided **minority** schools. *Pramati Educational Trust* (2014, five judges) held the Act does not apply to minority schools, aided or unaided. **India ratified the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child on 11 December 1992.** CRC adopted 20 Nov 1989; four principles: non-discrimination, best interests, survival and development, participation.

## RTE Act 2009 (निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य बाल शिक्षा का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2009)

**Act 35 of 2009**, assented 26 Aug 2009, in force **1 April 2010**. **7 chapters, 38 sections, 1 Schedule.** Amended in **2012** (CWSN, minority institutions), **2017** (teacher qualification deadline) and **2019** (no-detention).

### Definitions, s.2
- **s.2(c)** child = **6 to 14** years. **s.2(d)** child belonging to disadvantaged group (अलाभित समूह): SC, ST, socially and educationally backward, or other group disadvantaged by social, cultural, economic, geographical, linguistic or gender factors. **s.2(e)** weaker section (कमज़ोर वर्ग): parent's income below the limit notified by the appropriate Government.
- **s.2(ee)** child with disability (2012 amendment) links to the disability laws. **s.2(f)** elementary education = **Classes I to VIII**.
- **s.2(n)** four kinds of school: (i) Government or local authority, (ii) aided, (iii) **specified category** (Kendriya Vidyalaya, Navodaya, Sainik school), (iv) unaided.
- **s.1(4), (5)** (2012): the Act is subject to **Art 29 and 30** and does not apply to Madrasas, Vedic Pathsalas and institutions primarily imparting religious instruction.

### Rights and duties, s.3 to s.11
- **s.3**: every child 6–14 has the right to free and compulsory elementary education in a **neighbourhood school** (पड़ोस का विद्यालय). The 2012 proviso gives a child with severe or multiple disability the right to opt for **home-based education**.
- **s.4**: a child above 6 never admitted or who dropped out is admitted to an **age-appropriate class** and gets **special training** (विशेष प्रशिक्षण).
- **s.5**: right to seek transfer; the head teacher must issue the **Transfer Certificate immediately**; delay invites disciplinary action.
- **s.6**: neighbourhood school within **3 years** of commencement. Central Rules 2010 and Delhi Rules 2011 define neighbourhood as **1 km** walking distance for Classes I–V and **3 km** for Classes VI–VIII.
- **s.8** duties of appropriate Government; **s.9** duties of local authority (maintain records of children up to 14, ensure admission, monitor); **s.10** duty of parents to admit the child; **s.11** pre-school education for children above 3.

### Admission rules, s.12 to s.15
- **s.12(1)(c)**: unaided and specified-category schools must admit in **Class I** (or pre-primary where it exists) at least **25%** of strength from weaker section and disadvantaged group children of the neighbourhood and give them free education till Class VIII. **s.12(1)(b)**: aided schools give free education to a share of children proportionate to their aid, at least **25%**. **s.12(2)**: the State reimburses **unaided** schools at its **per-child expenditure or the fee actually charged, whichever is less**. In Delhi this quota is filled through the Directorate of Education's centralised computerised draw.
- **s.13**: no **capitation fee** (कैपिटेशन फीस) and no **screening procedure** (जांच प्रक्रिया) of child or parents. Penalty: capitation fee → fine **up to 10 times** the fee; screening → **₹25,000 first** contravention, **₹50,000 each subsequent** one.
- **s.14**: age proved by birth certificate under the **Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act 1886** or other prescribed document, but **no child can be denied admission for lack of age proof**.
- **s.15**: admission at the start of the academic year or within the extended period; even later admission cannot be denied.
- Supreme Court 2026: in *Lucknow Public School v. State of UP* (28 April 2026) the Court held schools must **admit children allotted under the 25% quota first** and raise eligibility disputes later; refusal violates Art 21A.

### Detention, punishment, recognition, s.16 to s.20
- **Original s.16**: no child shall be held back or expelled till completion of elementary education (the **no-detention policy**).
- **s.16 as substituted by the RTE (Amendment) Act 2019** (Act 1 of 2019, in force **1 March 2019**): (1) regular examination in **Class 5 and Class 8** at the end of every academic year; (2) a child who fails gets **additional instruction and a re-examination within 2 months** of the result; (3) the appropriate Government **may allow** schools to hold back the child in Class 5 or 8 or both; (4) **no child shall be expelled** till completion of elementary education. The Central RTE (Amendment) Rules of **December 2024** applied detention to Centre-run schools (KV, JNV, Sainik). About 16 States and 2 UTs had already ended no-detention under s.16(3) before these rules; check the latest DoE circular for Delhi's position.
- **s.17**: **no physical punishment or mental harassment** (शारीरिक दंड या मानसिक उत्पीड़न). Breach → **disciplinary action under the service rules** applicable to the person. There is no fine or jail term in s.17 itself. For Delhi, the Delhi High Court in *Parents Forum for Meaningful Education* (2000) struck down the corporal-punishment provision of Rule 37 of the Delhi School Education Rules 1973.
- **s.18**: no school without a **certificate of recognition**. Penalty: fine **up to ₹1 lakh**, and **₹10,000 per day** of continuing contravention. **s.19**: Schedule norms to be met within **3 years**; **s.20**: Central Government may amend the Schedule.

### SMC, teachers and curriculum, s.21 to s.30
- **s.21 School Management Committee** (विद्यालय प्रबंधन समिति): required in Government, local-authority, aided and specified-category schools, **not** in unaided schools. At least **three-fourths** of members are parents or guardians, with proportionate representation of disadvantaged and weaker-section parents; **50% women**. Functions: monitor the school, prepare the **School Development Plan (s.22)**, monitor grants. The 2012 amendment (s.21(3)) made the SMCs of **minority schools and all other aided schools advisory only**. Delhi reconstitutes SMCs through elections under DoE circulars.
- **s.23**: minimum qualifications laid down by the academic authority authorised by the Central Government, i.e. **NCTE**. The 2017 amendment gave untrained in-service teachers till **31 March 2019** to qualify. The Supreme Court in *Anjuman Ishaat-e-Taleem Trust* (September 2025; reviews dismissed in May 2026) made **TET mandatory** for in-service teachers to stay in service and to be promoted. The deadline is **31 August 2028**, extended under Art 142. Teachers with under 5 years of service left are exempt but cannot be promoted.
- **s.24** duties of teachers (regularity, completing curriculum, assessing each child, parent meetings). **s.25** pupil–teacher ratio. **s.26** teacher vacancies not to exceed **10%** of sanctioned strength.
- **s.27**: teachers cannot be deployed for non-educational work **except** the **decennial census, disaster relief, and elections** to local authority, State legislature or Parliament. **s.28**: no **private tuition**.
- **s.29**: curriculum and evaluation by the academic authority (NCERT nationally; **SCERT Delhi** was notified as the Academic Authority in 2013). Must follow constitutional values, all-round development, **activity and discovery based learning**, **mother tongue as medium as far as practicable**, freedom from fear and anxiety, and **comprehensive and continuous evaluation (CCE)** (सतत एवं व्यापक मूल्यांकन). **Learning outcomes** (अधिगम प्रतिफल) were added to the Central Rules in **2017**.
- **s.30**: no Board examination till completion of elementary education; a **certificate** on completion.

### Monitoring, s.31 to s.38
- **s.31**: **NCPCR** and **SCPCR** (in Delhi, **DCPCR**) monitor the child's right to education. **s.32**: grievance to the local authority, appeal to the SCPCR. **s.33 / s.34**: National and State Advisory Councils. **s.35**: Central Government may issue guidelines. **s.38**: rules (Central Rules **2010**, Delhi RTE Rules **2011**).

### The Schedule (norms and standards)

| Norm | Classes I–V | Classes VI–VIII |
|---|---|---|
| Pupil–teacher ratio | **30:1** (40:1 if above 200 children) | **35:1**, at least one teacher per subject group |
| Head teacher | above **150** children | above **100** children |
| Working days per year | **200** | **220** |
| Instructional hours per year | **800** | **1,000** |
| Teacher working hours | **45 per week** including preparation | same |

Building: all-weather, one classroom per teacher plus office-cum-store, **barrier-free access**, **separate toilets** for boys and girls, safe drinking water, kitchen for mid-day meal, playground, boundary wall, library, play material. A **2022 amendment** to the Schedule (29 Sept 2022) added pupil–teacher norms for special teachers in general schools.

## POCSO Act 2012 (लैंगिक अपराधों से बालकों का संरक्षण अधिनियम, 2012)

**Act 32 of 2012**, in force **14 November 2012** (Children's Day). **Gender-neutral**; child = any person **below 18** (s.2(1)(d)). Amended by **Act 25 of 2019** (in force 16 Aug 2019). **POCSO Rules 2020** replaced the 2012 Rules.

### Offences and punishments

| Offence | Sections | Punishment after 2019 |
|---|---|---|
| Penetrative sexual assault | s.3 / s.4 | Minimum **10 years** to life; if child below **16**, minimum **20 years** to life |
| Aggravated penetrative sexual assault | s.5 / s.6 | Minimum **20 years** to life, or **death** |
| Sexual assault | s.7 / s.8 | **3 to 5 years** |
| Aggravated sexual assault | s.9 / s.10 | **5 to 7 years** |
| Sexual harassment | s.11 / s.12 | up to **3 years** |
| Child for pornographic purposes | s.13 / s.14 | minimum 5 years (first), 7 years (subsequent) |
| Storage of child pornographic material | s.15 | graded: fine, up to 3 years, or 3–5 years if commercial |

"Aggravated" (s.5 and s.9) includes offences by a police officer, armed forces member, public servant, **management or staff of an educational institution or religious institution**, by a relative, gang, on a child below 12, or on a child with disability. **s.18**: attempt is punishable with up to half the punishment. **s.29**: presumption of guilt once prosecution proves foundational facts; **s.30**: presumption of culpable mental state.

### Reporting and procedure (what a school head must know)
- **s.19 mandatory reporting**: any person with knowledge or apprehension of an offence must report to the **Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU)** or **local police**. **s.21**: failure to report → up to **6 months** and/or fine. **s.21(2)**: a person **in charge of an institution** who fails to report an offence by a **subordinate** → up to **1 year** and fine. A **child** is not punished for not reporting. **s.22**: false complaint → up to 6 months; a child making a false complaint is not punished.
- **s.23**: media must not disclose the child's identity (6 months to 1 year). **s.24**: statement recorded at the child's **residence or place of choice**, as far as practicable by a **woman police officer not below Sub-Inspector**, **not in uniform**; the child is never kept in a police station at night. **s.26**: presence of parents or trusted person; special educator or interpreter for a child with disability; audio-video recording where possible. **s.27**: medical examination of a girl by a **woman doctor**, in the presence of a parent or trusted person.
- **s.28**: a **Court of Session** in each district is designated the **Special Court**; **s.32**: Special Public Prosecutor with 7 years' practice. **s.33**: child-friendly trial, in camera, no aggressive questioning, frequent breaks; **s.36**: child not to see the accused while testifying. **s.35**: evidence recorded within **30 days** of cognisance; trial completed within **1 year** as far as possible. **s.39**: guidelines for **support persons**. **s.43**: Government to spread awareness. **s.44**: **NCPCR/SCPCR** monitor implementation.
- **POCSO Rules 2020, Rule 3**: institutions housing or in regular contact with children, including **schools**, must carry out **periodic police verification and background checks of all staff**, train staff on child safety, and adopt a **child protection policy**. Rules also provide interim and final compensation to victims and mandatory reporting of child pornographic material.
- NCPCR's **POCSO e-Box** (2016) lets children complain online. Child helpline **1098**. In January 2026 the Supreme Court in *State of UP v. Anurudh* urged the Centre to consider a "Romeo–Juliet" clause for close-in-age adolescents; POCSO has **not** been amended.

## RPwD Act 2016 (दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016)

**Act 49 of 2016**, in force **19 April 2017**; replaced the PwD Act 1995 and gives effect to the **UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities** (ratified by India in 2007). Nodal: **DEPwD, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment**.

- **21 specified disabilities** in the Schedule (the 1995 Act had 7): blindness, low vision, leprosy cured, hearing impairment, locomotor disability, dwarfism, intellectual disability, mental illness, autism spectrum disorder, cerebral palsy, muscular dystrophy, chronic neurological conditions, **specific learning disabilities** (dyslexia, dysgraphia, dyscalculia, dyspraxia, developmental aphasia), multiple sclerosis, speech and language disability, thalassemia, haemophilia, sickle cell disease, multiple disabilities including deaf-blindness, **acid attack victims**, **Parkinson's disease**.
- **s.2(r) benchmark disability** (बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगता) = not less than **40%**. **s.2(m) inclusive education** (समावेशी शिक्षा) = students with and without disability learn together with teaching adapted to their needs. **s.2(y) reasonable accommodation** (युक्तियुक्त सुविधा).
- **s.16** duties of every educational institution funded or recognised by Government: admit without discrimination; accessible buildings and campus; reasonable accommodation; **individualised support**; education in appropriate languages and modes; **early detection of specific learning disabilities**; monitor participation; transport facilities.
- **s.17** specific measures: survey of school-going children **every 5 years** to identify CWSN; teacher training including **sign language and Braille**; resource centres; scholarships; **modified curriculum and exams** (extra time, scribe, exemption from second or third language).
- **s.31**: every child with benchmark disability aged **6 to 18** gets **free education** in a neighbourhood school or a special school of choice. **s.32**: at least **5%** of seats in Government and aided higher education institutions, with **5 years** upper-age relaxation. **s.34**: at least **4%** of posts in Government establishments (1% each for four categories of disability; the 1995 Act had 3%). **s.37**: 5% in poverty-alleviation and land schemes.
- Grievance and enforcement: **Chief Commissioner for PwD** (s.74), **State Commissioner** (s.79), **Special Courts** (s.84, Court of Session), **certificate of disability** (s.58), now issued through the **UDID** system. **s.92**: atrocities against PwD → 6 months to 5 years.
- Delhi-relevant: NEP 2020 (Chapter 6, Equitable and Inclusive Education) and **Samagra Shiksha** fund CWSN in Classes pre-primary to XII through identification camps, aids and appliances, Braille books, **escort and transport allowance**, a **stipend for girls with disabilities**, home-based education and resource rooms. 3 December is International Day of Persons with Disabilities; Accessible India Campaign (Sugamya Bharat) launched 3 Dec 2015.

## Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act 2015 (किशोर न्याय अधिनियम, 2015)

**Act 2 of 2016**, in force **15 January 2016**, replacing the JJ Act 2000. Amended by the **JJ (Amendment) Act 2021** (in force 1 Sept 2022). Nodal: **Ministry of Women and Child Development**.

- Two groups: **child in conflict with law** (विधि का उल्लंघन करने वाला बालक, s.2(13)) and **child in need of care and protection** (देखरेख और संरक्षण की आवश्यकता वाला बालक, s.2(14)). Child = below **18** (s.2(12)).
- Offence grades: **petty** (up to 3 years), **serious** (3–7 years), **heinous** (minimum **7 years or more**). The 2021 amendment treats offences with a maximum above 7 years and no minimum, or a minimum below 7 years, as serious.
- **Juvenile Justice Board (किशोर न्याय बोर्ड), s.4**: a Metropolitan or Judicial Magistrate First Class plus **two social workers, at least one a woman**. **Child Welfare Committee (बाल कल्याण समिति), s.27**: chairperson plus **four members**, at least one woman.
- **s.15 preliminary assessment**: for a child aged **16–18** accused of a **heinous** offence, the Board assesses mental and physical capacity and understanding within **3 months**; it may transfer the case to the **Children's Court** (s.18(3), s.19). **s.21**: no child in conflict with law may be sentenced to **death or life imprisonment without possibility of release**.
- **s.74**: identity of any child must not be disclosed by media (up to 6 months and/or ₹2 lakh). **s.75**: cruelty to a child → up to 3 years and/or ₹1 lakh; if by a person in charge of or employed by an organisation entrusted with the child → up to **5 years** and ₹5 lakh. **s.82**: **corporal punishment in a child care institution** → ₹10,000 fine on first conviction, imprisonment up to 3 months on later ones. **s.85**: offences against a child with disability carry **double** punishment.
- Adoption: **CARA** is statutory (s.68); the 2021 amendment transferred power to issue adoption orders from courts to the **District Magistrate**. DMs also gained wider powers to oversee child care institutions and child protection bodies in the district, and registration of child care institutions now needs the DM's recommendation.
- Institutions: Observation Home, Special Home, Place of Safety (for children in conflict with law); Children's Home, Open Shelter, Specialised Adoption Agency (for children in need of care). After-care up to **21 years**.

## Related laws and bodies in one place

| Law or body | Key fact |
|---|---|
| CPCR Act 2005 | **NCPCR** set up March 2007; chairperson + 6 members; monitors RTE (s.31) and POCSO (s.44). **DCPCR** for Delhi |
| Prohibition of Child Marriage Act 2006 | Child = girl below **18**, boy below **21**; marriage **voidable**; adult male marrying a child → up to 2 years RI and/or ₹1 lakh |
| Child and Adolescent Labour Act 1986 (amended 2016) | No child **below 14** in any occupation (except family enterprise after school and audio-visual entertainment); adolescents **14–18** barred from hazardous work; **PENCIL** portal |
| School safety | MoE Guidelines on School Safety and Security **2021** fix accountability of the head of school and management; NCPCR Manual on Safety and Security; NCPCR guidelines on preventing bullying and cyberbullying 2024 |
| Mission Vatsalya | Umbrella child-protection scheme of MWCD (from 2021-22), with Childline 1098 |

## Common traps

- **Age limits**: RTE 6–14; RPwD free education **6–18**; POCSO and JJ child **below 18**; child labour ban below 14, adolescents 14–18; PCMA girl 18, boy **21**; JJ preliminary assessment **16–18**.
- **Dates**: RTE enacted 2009 but in force **1 April 2010**; 2019 amendment in force **1 March 2019**; POCSO in force **14 Nov 2012**; RPwD in force **19 April 2017**; JJ Act 2015 in force **15 Jan 2016**.
- **s.16 after 2019** does not restore expulsion. Detention is only "may", by the appropriate Government, only in Classes 5 and 8, only after the re-exam.
- **s.17 penalty** is disciplinary action under service rules, not a fine. The fines in s.13 and s.18 are for schools, not teachers.
- **SMC**: three-fourths parents, half women, not required in unaided schools; SMCs of minority and all aided schools are advisory only.
- **25% quota** under s.12(1)(c) applies to unaided and specified-category schools, not Government or minority schools; aided schools admit free in proportion to aid (minimum 25%) under s.12(1)(b). Reimbursement goes to unaided schools and is the **lower** of per-child cost and fee.
- **Non-educational duties allowed**: census, disaster relief, elections. Polio drives, surveys and board-exam work are not in s.27.
- **POCSO reporting**: 6 months for anyone, **1 year** for an institution head who ignores a subordinate's offence. The report goes to SJPU or police, not to the CWC or the Principal only.
- **Aggravated** offences include those by **school staff** and on children below 12. Death penalty only under s.6, not s.4.
- **Numbers**: RPwD 21 disabilities, 40% benchmark, 4% posts, 5% HE seats; 1995 Act had 7 disabilities and 3%.
- **Bodies**: JJB for children in conflict with law; CWC for children in need of care; Special Court for POCSO is a Sessions Court; NCPCR monitors both RTE and POCSO.

## Remember for the exam

1. Art 21A, Art 45 (substituted) and Art 51A(k): all three from the 86th Amendment 2002; Art 21A in force 1 April 2010.
2. RTE Act 35 of 2009: 7 chapters, 38 sections, 1 Schedule; child 6–14; elementary = Classes I–VIII.
3. s.12(1)(c): 25% of Class I seats in unaided and specified-category schools.
4. s.13: capitation fee up to 10 times; screening ₹25,000 then ₹50,000. s.18: ₹1 lakh plus ₹10,000 per day.
5. s.16 (2019): exam in Classes 5 and 8, re-exam within 2 months, detention allowed by appropriate Government, no expulsion.
6. s.17: no physical punishment or mental harassment; disciplinary action under service rules.
7. s.21 SMC: three-fourths parents, 50% women; s.22 School Development Plan.
8. s.27: census, disaster relief, elections only; s.28: no private tuition.
9. Schedule: PTR 30:1 and 35:1; 200/220 days; 800/1,000 hours; 45 hours a week.
10. POCSO: child below 18, gender-neutral, in force 14 Nov 2012, Rules 2020; s.19 report to SJPU or police; s.21 up to 6 months, institution head up to 1 year.
11. POCSO s.35: evidence in 30 days, trial in 1 year; Special Court = Court of Session.
12. RPwD 2016: 21 disabilities, 40% benchmark, free education 6–18, 5% HE seats, 4% posts, survey every 5 years.
13. JJ Act 2015: JJB (Magistrate + 2 social workers), CWC (chair + 4); heinous = 7 years or more; preliminary assessment for 16–18; no death or life without release.
14. JJ s.82: corporal punishment in a child care institution; s.75: cruelty by an organisation employee up to 5 years.
15. NCPCR (2007, CPCR Act 2005) monitors RTE s.31 and POCSO s.44; DCPCR in Delhi; Childline 1098.
quick_facts: RTE Act 2009 (Act 35 of 2009) came into force on 1 April 2010, the same day as Art 21A; it has 7 chapters, 38 sections and 1 Schedule.
RTE child = 6 to 14 years; elementary education = Classes I to VIII; neighbourhood = 1 km (I–V) and 3 km (VI–VIII) under the Rules.

s.12(1)(c): unaided and specified-category schools admit at least 25% weaker-section and disadvantaged children in Class I; unaided schools are reimbursed at the lower of per-child cost and fee (s.12(2)).
s.13 penalties: capitation fee up to 10 times the fee; screening ₹25,000 first and ₹50,000 each subsequent contravention. s.18: up to ₹1 lakh plus ₹10,000 per day.
s.16 (substituted 2019, in force 1 March 2019): regular exam in Classes 5 and 8, re-exam within 2 months, appropriate Government may allow detention, no expulsion till Class VIII.
s.17: no physical punishment or mental harassment; breach leads to disciplinary action under the service rules.
s.21 SMC: at least three-fourths parents or guardians, 50% women; not required in unaided schools; SMCs of minority schools and all other aided schools are advisory only (s.21(3), 2012).
s.27: teachers deployed only for decennial census, disaster relief and elections; s.28 bars private tuition.
RTE Schedule: PTR 30:1 (I–V) and 35:1 (VI–VIII); 200/220 working days; 800/1,000 instructional hours; 45 teacher hours a week.
POCSO 2012 (in force 14 Nov 2012): gender-neutral, child below 18; 2019 amendment raised minimum under s.4 to 20 years for victims below 16 and added death penalty under s.6.
POCSO s.19 mandatory reporting to SJPU or local police; s.21 non-reporting up to 6 months, institution head ignoring a subordinate's offence up to 1 year; child never punished.
POCSO s.24: statement at child's residence by a woman officer not below Sub-Inspector, not in uniform; s.35: evidence within 30 days, trial within 1 year; Special Court = Court of Session.
RPwD Act 2016 (in force 19 April 2017): 21 disabilities, benchmark 40%, free education 6–18 (s.31), 5% HE seats (s.32), 4% Government posts (s.34), CWSN survey every 5 years (s.17).

JJ Act 2015 (in force 15 Jan 2016): JJB = Magistrate + 2 social workers; CWC = chair + 4; heinous offence = 7 years or more; preliminary assessment for 16–18 (s.15); no death or life without release (s.21).
NCPCR (2007, under CPCR Act 2005) monitors RTE (s.31) and POCSO (s.44); DCPCR is Delhi's commission; Childline number is 1098.

mcqs.q_en: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 came into force on:
mcqs.q_hi: निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य बाल शिक्षा का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2009 किस तिथि से लागू हुआ?
mcqs.explain_en: The RTE Act received assent in August 2009 but was brought into force on 1 April 2010, the same day Art 21A commenced. 1 March 2019 is when the no-detention amendment took effect, and 14 November 2012 is the POCSO commencement date.
mcqs.explain_hi: RTE अधिनियम को अगस्त 2009 में स्वीकृति मिली, पर यह 1 अप्रैल 2010 से लागू हुआ, उसी दिन अनुच्छेद 21A भी प्रभावी हुआ। 1 मार्च 2019 नो-डिटेंशन संशोधन की तिथि है और 14 नवंबर 2012 पॉक्सो अधिनियम के लागू होने की तिथि है।
mcqs.source: RTE Act 2009, s.1(3); notification bringing Act and Art 21A into force on 1 April 2010

mcqs.q_en:
Consider the following statements about Section 12 of the RTE Act, 2009:
1. Clause (1)(c) applies to unaided schools and to specified-category schools such as Kendriya Vidyalayas.
2. At least 25% of the strength of Class I must be admitted from weaker-section and disadvantaged-group children of the neighbourhood.
3. The State reimburses an unaided school at its per-child expenditure or the actual fee charged, whichever is less.
4. Clause (1)(c) applies equally to unaided minority schools.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.q_hi:
RTE अधिनियम, 2009 की धारा 12 के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
1. खंड (1)(c) गैर-सहायता प्राप्त विद्यालयों और केंद्रीय विद्यालय जैसे विनिर्दिष्ट श्रेणी के विद्यालयों पर लागू होता है।
2. कक्षा I की संख्या के कम से कम 25% में पड़ोस के कमज़ोर वर्ग और अलाभित समूह के बच्चों को प्रवेश देना होगा।
3. राज्य गैर-सहायता प्राप्त विद्यालय को अपने प्रति-बालक व्यय या वास्तव में लिए गए शुल्क, जो भी कम हो, की प्रतिपूर्ति करता है।
4. खंड (1)(c) गैर-सहायता प्राप्त अल्पसंख्यक विद्यालयों पर समान रूप से लागू होता है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?
mcqs.explain_en: Statements 1, 2 and 3 restate s.12(1)(c) and s.12(2); the s.12(2) reimbursement is for unaided schools (s.2(n)(iv)). Statement 4 is wrong: s.1(4) makes the Act subject to Art 29 and 30, and the Supreme Court in Pramati (2014) held the Act does not apply to minority schools, aided or unaided.
mcqs.explain_hi: कथन 1, 2 और 3 धारा 12(1)(c) और 12(2) के अनुरूप हैं; धारा 12(2) की प्रतिपूर्ति गैर-सहायता प्राप्त विद्यालयों (धारा 2(n)(iv)) के लिए है। कथन 4 गलत है: धारा 1(4) अधिनियम को अनुच्छेद 29 और 30 के अधीन बनाती है और प्रमति (2014) निर्णय में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने कहा कि यह अधिनियम अल्पसंख्यक विद्यालयों, सहायता प्राप्त या गैर-सहायता प्राप्त, पर लागू नहीं होता।
mcqs.source: RTE Act 2009, s.12(1)(c), s.12(2), s.1(4); Pramati Educational & Cultural Trust v. Union of India (2014)

mcqs.q_en: Under Section 13 of the RTE Act, 2009, a school that subjects a child or parents to a screening procedure for admission is liable to a fine of:
mcqs.q_hi: RTE अधिनियम, 2009 की धारा 13 के अंतर्गत, प्रवेश के लिए बालक या माता-पिता को जांच प्रक्रिया (स्क्रीनिंग) के अधीन करने वाला विद्यालय कितने जुर्माने का भागी होगा?
options_en: ₹25,000 for the first contravention and ₹50,000 for each subsequent contravention
Up to ten times the fee charged
Up to ₹1 lakh and ₹10,000 per day of continuing contravention
₹5,000 for the first contravention and ₹10,000 for each subsequent contravention
options_hi: पहले उल्लंघन पर ₹25,000 और प्रत्येक बाद के उल्लंघन पर ₹50,000
लिए गए शुल्क का दस गुना तक
₹1 लाख तक और निरंतर उल्लंघन पर ₹10,000 प्रतिदिन
पहले उल्लंघन पर ₹5,000 और प्रत्येक बाद के उल्लंघन पर ₹10,000
mcqs.explain_en: s.13(2)(b) prescribes ₹25,000 for the first and ₹50,000 for each subsequent screening contravention. Ten times the fee is the capitation-fee penalty under s.13(2)(a), and ₹1 lakh plus ₹10,000 per day is the s.18 penalty for running a school without recognition.
mcqs.explain_hi: धारा 13(2)(b) में स्क्रीनिंग के पहले उल्लंघन पर ₹25,000 और प्रत्येक बाद के उल्लंघन पर ₹50,000 का प्रावधान है। शुल्क का दस गुना कैपिटेशन फीस का दंड है (धारा 13(2)(a)) और ₹1 लाख तथा ₹10,000 प्रतिदिन धारा 18 के अंतर्गत बिना मान्यता विद्यालय चलाने का दंड है।

mcqs.q_en:
Consider the following statements about Section 16 of the RTE Act as substituted by the RTE (Amendment) Act, 2019:
1. There shall be a regular examination in Class 5 and Class 8 at the end of every academic year.
2. A child who fails shall be given additional instruction and a re-examination within two months of the declaration of the result.
3. The appropriate Government may allow schools to hold back a child in Class 5 or Class 8 or both if the child fails the re-examination.
4. A child who fails the re-examination may be expelled from the school.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.q_hi:
RTE (संशोधन) अधिनियम, 2019 द्वारा प्रतिस्थापित धारा 16 के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
1. प्रत्येक शैक्षणिक वर्ष के अंत में कक्षा 5 और कक्षा 8 में नियमित परीक्षा होगी।
2. अनुत्तीर्ण बालक को अतिरिक्त अनुदेश दिया जाएगा और परिणाम घोषणा के दो माह के भीतर पुनः परीक्षा का अवसर मिलेगा।
3. समुचित सरकार विद्यालयों को पुनः परीक्षा में अनुत्तीर्ण बालक को कक्षा 5 या कक्षा 8 या दोनों में रोकने की अनुमति दे सकती है।
4. पुनः परीक्षा में अनुत्तीर्ण बालक को विद्यालय से निष्कासित किया जा सकता है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?
mcqs.explain_en: Statements 1 to 3 reproduce s.16(1) to (3). Statement 4 is the trap: s.16(4) expressly says no child shall be expelled from any school till the completion of elementary education, so the 2019 amendment allowed detention but never expulsion.
mcqs.explain_hi: कथन 1 से 3 धारा 16(1) से (3) के अनुरूप हैं। कथन 4 गलत है: धारा 16(4) स्पष्ट कहती है कि प्रारंभिक शिक्षा पूरी होने तक किसी बालक को विद्यालय से निष्कासित नहीं किया जाएगा, अर्थात 2019 संशोधन ने रोकने की अनुमति दी, निष्कासन की नहीं।
mcqs.source: RTE (Amendment) Act 2019 (Act 1 of 2019), substituted s.16(1)–(4); in force 1 March 2019 (S.O. 1044(E), 28.02.2019)

mcqs.q_en: Under Section 27 of the RTE Act, 2009, a teacher may NOT be deployed for which of the following purposes?
mcqs.q_hi: RTE अधिनियम, 2009 की धारा 27 के अंतर्गत शिक्षक को निम्नलिखित में से किस कार्य के लिए तैनात नहीं किया जा सकता?
options_en: Elections to Parliament or the State Legislature
options_hi: संसद या राज्य विधानमंडल के चुनाव
mcqs.explain_en: s.27 bars deployment of teachers for non-educational purposes except the decennial census, disaster relief and elections to the local authority, State Legislature or Parliament. Health drives and other surveys are not in the list.
mcqs.explain_hi: धारा 27 शिक्षकों को गैर-शैक्षिक कार्यों में लगाने पर रोक लगाती है, केवल दशवार्षिक जनगणना, आपदा राहत और स्थानीय प्राधिकरण, राज्य विधानमंडल या संसद के चुनावों को छोड़कर। स्वास्थ्य अभियान और अन्य सर्वेक्षण इस सूची में नहीं हैं।

mcqs.q_en:
Match the norms in the Schedule to the RTE Act, 2009:
List I: A. Pupil–teacher ratio, Classes I–V; B. Pupil–teacher ratio, Classes VI–VIII; C. Working days per year, Classes VI–VIII; D. Instructional hours per year, Classes I–V
List II: 1. 30:1; 2. 220; 3. 35:1; 4. 800
Select the correct code.
mcqs.q_hi:
RTE अधिनियम, 2009 की अनुसूची के मानकों का मिलान कीजिए:
सूची I: A. छात्र-शिक्षक अनुपात, कक्षा I–V; B. छात्र-शिक्षक अनुपात, कक्षा VI–VIII; C. प्रति वर्ष कार्य दिवस, कक्षा VI–VIII; D. प्रति वर्ष अनुदेश घंटे, कक्षा I–V
सूची II: 1. 30:1; 2. 220; 3. 35:1; 4. 800
सही कूट चुनिए।
mcqs.explain_en: The Schedule fixes PTR 30:1 for Classes I–V and 35:1 for VI–VIII, 200 and 220 working days, and 800 and 1,000 instructional hours respectively. The wrong codes swap the two PTRs or confuse days with hours.
mcqs.explain_hi: अनुसूची में कक्षा I–V के लिए 30:1 और VI–VIII के लिए 35:1 अनुपात, क्रमशः 200 और 220 कार्य दिवस तथा 800 और 1,000 अनुदेश घंटे निर्धारित हैं। गलत कूट दोनों अनुपातों को बदल देते हैं या दिवसों और घंटों में भ्रम पैदा करते हैं।
mcqs.source: RTE Act 2009, Schedule (norms and standards for a school), items 1, 3 and 4

mcqs.q_en:
Consider the following statements about the School Management Committee (SMC) under Section 21 of the RTE Act, 2009:
1. At least three-fourths of its members must be parents or guardians.
2. Fifty per cent of its members must be women.
3. Every unaided private school must also constitute an SMC.
4. The SMC of an aided minority school performs advisory functions only.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.q_hi:
RTE अधिनियम, 2009 की धारा 21 के अंतर्गत विद्यालय प्रबंधन समिति (SMC) के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
1. इसके कम से कम तीन-चौथाई सदस्य माता-पिता या अभिभावक होने चाहिए।
2. इसके पचास प्रतिशत सदस्य महिलाएँ होनी चाहिए।
3. प्रत्येक गैर-सहायता प्राप्त निजी विद्यालय को भी SMC गठित करनी होगी।
4. सहायता प्राप्त अल्पसंख्यक विद्यालय की SMC केवल सलाहकारी कार्य करती है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?
mcqs.explain_en: s.21(1) requires an SMC in every school other than an unaided school (s.2(n)(iv)), with three-fourths parents and 50% women. s.21(3), inserted in 2012, makes the SMCs of minority schools and of all other aided schools advisory only, so statement 4 is correct. Statement 3 is wrong.
mcqs.explain_hi: धारा 21(1) गैर-सहायता प्राप्त विद्यालय (धारा 2(n)(iv)) को छोड़कर हर विद्यालय में SMC अनिवार्य करती है, जिसमें तीन-चौथाई माता-पिता और 50% महिलाएँ हों। 2012 में जोड़ी गई धारा 21(3) के अनुसार अल्पसंख्यक विद्यालयों और अन्य सभी सहायता प्राप्त विद्यालयों की SMC केवल सलाहकारी कार्य करती है, अतः कथन 4 सही है। कथन 3 गलत है।
mcqs.source: RTE Act 2009, s.21(1) and s.21(3) inserted by RTE (Amendment) Act 2012; s.2(n)(iv)

mcqs.q_en: Under Section 21 of the POCSO Act, 2012, a person in charge of an institution who fails to report an offence committed by a subordinate under their control is punishable with imprisonment up to:
mcqs.q_hi: पॉक्सो अधिनियम, 2012 की धारा 21 के अंतर्गत, किसी संस्था का प्रभारी व्यक्ति जो अपने नियंत्रणाधीन अधीनस्थ द्वारा किए गए अपराध की रिपोर्ट करने में विफल रहता है, उसे अधिकतम कितने कारावास से दंडित किया जा सकता है?
mcqs.explain_en: s.21(2) prescribes up to one year and fine for the head of a company or institution who fails to report a subordinate's offence; s.21(1) gives up to six months for any other person. Three years is the s.12 sexual-harassment maximum.
mcqs.explain_hi: धारा 21(2) में किसी कंपनी या संस्था के प्रभारी द्वारा अधीनस्थ के अपराध की रिपोर्ट न करने पर एक वर्ष तक का कारावास और जुर्माना है; धारा 21(1) में अन्य किसी व्यक्ति के लिए छह माह तक है। तीन वर्ष धारा 12 के अंतर्गत लैंगिक उत्पीड़न की अधिकतम सज़ा है।
mcqs.source: POCSO Act 2012, s.19, s.21(1) and s.21(2)

mcqs.q_en:
Assertion (A): A sexual offence committed by a teacher on a student of the same school is treated as an 'aggravated' offence under the POCSO Act, 2012.
Reason (R): Sections 5 and 9 of the POCSO Act list offences committed by a person on the management or staff of an educational institution on a child in that institution as aggravated penetrative sexual assault and aggravated sexual assault respectively.
Select the correct answer.
mcqs.q_hi:
अभिकथन (A): किसी शिक्षक द्वारा उसी विद्यालय के विद्यार्थी के साथ किया गया लैंगिक अपराध पॉक्सो अधिनियम, 2012 के अंतर्गत 'गुरुतर' अपराध माना जाता है।
कारण (R): पॉक्सो अधिनियम की धारा 5 और 9 शैक्षणिक संस्था के प्रबंधन या कर्मचारी द्वारा उस संस्था के बालक पर किए गए अपराध को क्रमशः गुरुतर प्रवेशन लैंगिक हमला और गुरुतर लैंगिक हमला के रूप में सूचीबद्ध करती हैं।
सही उत्तर चुनिए।
options_en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
options_hi: A और R दोनों सत्य हैं, और R, A की सही व्याख्या है
A और R दोनों सत्य हैं, किंतु R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है
A सत्य है, किंतु R असत्य है
A असत्य है, किंतु R सत्य है
mcqs.explain_en: Clause (f) of both s.5 and s.9 covers whoever, being on the management or staff of an educational institution, commits the offence on a child in that institution; this is exactly why the teacher's offence is aggravated, attracting s.6 (20 years to life or death) or s.10 (5 to 7 years).
mcqs.explain_hi: धारा 5 और 9 दोनों का खंड (f) शैक्षणिक संस्था के प्रबंधन या कर्मचारी द्वारा उस संस्था के बालक पर किए गए अपराध को शामिल करता है; यही कारण है कि शिक्षक का अपराध गुरुतर माना जाता है और धारा 6 (20 वर्ष से आजीवन या मृत्युदंड) या धारा 10 (5 से 7 वर्ष) लागू होती है।
mcqs.source: POCSO Act 2012, s.5(f), s.6, s.9(f), s.10 (as amended 2019)

mcqs.q_en:
Consider the following statements about procedure under the POCSO Act, 2012:
1. The statement of the child is to be recorded at the residence of the child or at a place of the child's choice.
2. As far as practicable, the statement is recorded by a woman police officer not below the rank of Sub-Inspector.
3. The police officer recording the statement should not be in uniform.
4. The Special Court should record the child's evidence within 30 days of taking cognisance and complete the trial, as far as possible, within one year.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.q_hi:
पॉक्सो अधिनियम, 2012 के अंतर्गत प्रक्रिया के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
1. बालक का कथन उसके निवास पर या उसकी पसंद के स्थान पर अभिलिखित किया जाएगा।
2. यथासंभव, कथन उप-निरीक्षक से नीचे की रैंक की न होने वाली महिला पुलिस अधिकारी द्वारा अभिलिखित किया जाएगा।
3. कथन अभिलिखित करने वाला पुलिस अधिकारी वर्दी में नहीं होना चाहिए।
4. विशेष न्यायालय को संज्ञान लेने के 30 दिनों के भीतर बालक का साक्ष्य अभिलिखित करना चाहिए और यथासंभव एक वर्ष के भीतर विचारण पूरा करना चाहिए।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?
mcqs.explain_en: Statements 1 to 3 come from s.24(1) and s.24(2), and statement 4 from s.35(1) and s.35(2). All four are correct, so the trap is the candidate who doubts one and picks a narrower option.
mcqs.explain_hi: कथन 1 से 3 धारा 24(1) और 24(2) से तथा कथन 4 धारा 35(1) और 35(2) से लिए गए हैं। चारों सही हैं, अतः जो अभ्यर्थी किसी एक पर संदेह कर संकुचित विकल्प चुनता है वह गलत हो जाता है।

mcqs.q_en: Under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, the number of specified disabilities in the Schedule and the minimum percentage for 'benchmark disability' are respectively:
mcqs.q_hi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 के अंतर्गत अनुसूची में निर्दिष्ट दिव्यांगताओं की संख्या और 'बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगता' के लिए न्यूनतम प्रतिशत क्रमशः हैं:
mcqs.explain_en: The RPwD Act 2016 Schedule lists 21 specified disabilities and s.2(r) defines benchmark disability as not less than 40%. Seven was the count under the repealed PwD Act 1995.
mcqs.explain_hi: RPwD अधिनियम 2016 की अनुसूची में 21 निर्दिष्ट दिव्यांगताएँ हैं और धारा 2(r) बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगता को 40% से कम नहीं के रूप में परिभाषित करती है। सात की संख्या निरसित PwD अधिनियम 1995 के अंतर्गत थी।
mcqs.source: RPwD Act 2016, s.2(r) and the Schedule

mcqs.q_en:
Consider the following statements about the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016:
1. Every child with benchmark disability between 6 and 18 years has the right to free education in a neighbourhood school or a special school of choice.
2. The appropriate Government must conduct a survey of school-going children every five years to identify children with disabilities.
3. Government and aided higher education institutions must reserve at least 5% of seats for persons with benchmark disabilities.
4. Government establishments must reserve at least 3% of posts for persons with benchmark disabilities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.q_hi:
दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
1. 6 से 18 वर्ष के बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगता वाले प्रत्येक बालक को पड़ोस के विद्यालय या अपनी पसंद के विशेष विद्यालय में निःशुल्क शिक्षा का अधिकार है।
2. समुचित सरकार को दिव्यांग बालकों की पहचान के लिए प्रत्येक पाँच वर्ष में विद्यालय जाने वाले बालकों का सर्वेक्षण करना होगा।
3. सरकारी और सहायता प्राप्त उच्च शिक्षा संस्थानों को बेंचमार्क दिव्य���ंगजन के लिए कम से कम 5% सीटें आरक्षित करनी होंगी।
4. सरकारी प्रतिष्ठानों को बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगजन के लिए कम से कम 3% पद आरक्षित करने होंगे।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?
mcqs.explain_en: s.31 (free education 6–18), s.17(a) (survey every five years) and s.32 (5% in higher education) are correct. Statement 4 is wrong because s.34 fixes not less than 4% of posts; 3% was the figure under the 1995 Act.
mcqs.explain_hi: धारा 31 (6–18 वर्ष निःशुल्क शिक्षा), धारा 17(a) (हर पाँच वर्ष में सर्वेक्षण) और धारा 32 (उच्च शिक्षा में 5%) सही हैं। कथन 4 गलत है क्योंकि धारा 34 पदों में 4% से कम नहीं निर्धारित करती है; 3% का आंकड़ा 1995 के अधिनियम का था।

mcqs.topic: JJ Act 2015 children in conflict with law
mcqs.q_en:
Consider the following statements about the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015:
1. A 'heinous offence' is one for which the minimum punishment under any law is imprisonment for seven years or more.
2. For a child aged 16 to 18 alleged to have committed a heinous offence, the Juvenile Justice Board conducts a preliminary assessment of the child's mental and physical capacity and understanding.
3. A child in conflict with law who is tried as an adult may be sentenced to death.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.q_hi:
किशोर न्याय (बालकों की देखरेख और संरक्षण) अधिनियम, 2015 के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
1. 'जघन्य अपराध' वह है जिसके लिए किसी विधि के अंतर्गत न्यूनतम दंड सात वर्ष या अधिक का कारावास हो।
2. जघन्य अपराध के आरोपी 16 से 18 वर्ष के बालक के लिए किशोर न्याय बोर्ड उसकी मानसिक और शारीरिक क्षमता तथा समझ का प्रारंभिक आकलन करता है।
3. वयस्क के रूप में विचारित विधि का उल्लंघन करने वाले बालक को मृत्युदंड दिया जा सकता है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
mcqs.explain_en: s.2(33) defines heinous offences as those with a minimum of seven years or more, and s.15 provides the preliminary assessment for 16–18-year-olds. Statement 3 is wrong: s.21 bars any sentence of death or life imprisonment without the possibility of release for a child in conflict with law.
mcqs.explain_hi: धारा 2(33) जघन्य अपराध को सात वर्ष या अधिक के न्यूनतम दंड वाले अपराध के रूप में परिभाषित करती है, और धारा 15 में 16–18 वर्ष के बालकों के लिए प्रारंभिक आकलन का प्रावधान है। कथन 3 गलत है: धारा 21 विधि का उल्लंघन करने वाले बालक को मृत्युदंड या रिहाई की संभावना के बिना आजीवन कारावास देने पर रोक लगाती है।

mcqs.q_en:
Match the following bodies with their role:
List I: A. Juvenile Justice Board; B. Child Welfare Committee; C. Special Court under the POCSO Act; D. Special Juvenile Police Unit
List II: 1. A Court of Session designated for each district; 2. Deals with children in need of care and protection; 3. Deals with children in conflict with law; 4. Receives reports of offences under Section 19 of the POCSO Act
Select the correct code.
mcqs.q_hi:
निम्नलिखित निकायों का उनकी भूमिका से मिलान कीजिए:
सूची I: A. किशोर न्याय बोर्ड; B. बाल कल्याण समिति; C. पॉक्सो अधिनियम के अंतर्गत विशेष न्यायालय; D. विशेष किशोर पुलिस इकाई
सूची II: 1. प्रत्येक जिले के लिए नामित सत्र न्यायालय; 2. देखरेख और संरक्षण की आवश्यकता वाले बालकों से संबंधित; 3. विधि का उल्लंघन करने वाले बालकों से संबंधित; 4. पॉक्सो अधिनियम की धारा 19 के अंतर्गत अपराधों की रिपोर्ट प्राप्त करती है
सही कूट चुनिए।
mcqs.explain_en: The JJB (JJ Act s.4) handles children in conflict with law and the CWC (s.27) children in need of care and protection; POCSO s.28 designates a Court of Session as the Special Court and s.19 directs reports to the SJPU or local police. The wrong codes swap JJB with CWC or the court with the police unit.
mcqs.explain_hi: किशोर न्याय बोर्ड (JJ अधिनियम धारा 4) विधि का उल्लंघन करने वाले बालकों और बाल कल्याण समिति (धारा 27) देखरेख की आवश्यकता वाले बालकों से संबंधित है; पॉक्सो धारा 28 सत्र न्यायालय को विशेष न्यायालय नामित करती है और धारा 19 रिपोर्ट SJPU या स्थानीय पुलिस को देने का निर्देश देती है। गलत कूट JJB और CWC या न्यायालय और पुलिस इकाई को बदल देते हैं।
mcqs.source: JJ Act 2015, s.4 and s.27; POCSO Act 2012, s.19 and s.28

mcqs.q_en: Under Section 17 of the RTE Act, 2009, a person who subjects a child to physical punishment or mental harassment is liable to:
mcqs.q_hi: RTE अधिनियम, 2009 की धारा 17 के अंतर्गत, बालक को शारीरिक दंड या मानसिक उत्पीड़न देने वाला व्यक्ति किसका भागी होगा?
options_en: Disciplinary action under the service rules applicable to such person
options_hi: उस व्यक्ति पर लागू सेवा नियमों के अंतर्गत अनुशासनात्मक कार्रवाई
mcqs.explain_en: s.17(2) provides only disciplinary action under the service rules applicable to the person. The fine of ₹25,000 is the s.13 screening penalty, and withdrawal of recognition is a s.18 consequence for the school, not the teacher.
mcqs.explain_hi: धारा 17(2) में केवल उस व्यक्ति पर लागू सेवा नियमों के अंतर्गत अनुशासनात्मक कार्रवाई का प्रावधान है। ₹25,000 का जुर्माना धारा 13 के स्क्रीनिंग उल्लंघन का दंड है, और मान्यता वापस लेना धारा 18 के अंतर्गत विद्यालय के लिए परिणाम है, शिक्षक के लिए नहीं।

changes: All 15 keys solved independently before checking: all 15 agree with the given keys. No key changed. Answer spread stays 4/4/4/3.

Q2: statement 3 now says 'an unaided school', because the s.12(2) reimbursement applies only to s.2(n)(iv) unaided schools, not to KVs. Statements 1 and 4 now name clause (1)(c). Key unchanged (B). Hindi and explanation updated to match.

Q7: explanation corrected. s.21(3), inserted in 2012, makes the SMCs of minority schools AND all other aided schools advisory, not only aided minority schools. Statement 4 is still true; key unchanged (C). Hindi updated.
Q14 Hindi: fixed the garbled character in 'विशेष किशोर पुलिस इकाई'.
Q4 source: added the commencement notification S.O. 1044(E) dated 28.02.2019 (1 March 2019 confirmed in research/02).
Reading s.14: the Act named was wrong. 'Registration of Births and Deaths Act 1886' → 'Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act 1886' (the 1969 Act is a different law).

Reading s.12: s.12(2) reimbursement now says it goes to unaided schools. Added s.12(1)(b): aided schools admit free in proportion to their aid, minimum 25%. 'Common traps' and quick fact 3 updated to match.

Reading s.12: removed 'January 2026 SC called the quota a national mission'. It is tagged [CHECK] in research/05 with only a non-official source, and I could not verify it. Lucknow Public School (28 Apr 2026, [OFF]) is kept.

Reading s.16: 'Most States and UTs, including Delhi, had already ended no-detention' → 'About 16 States and 2 UTs …; check the latest DoE circular for Delhi's position'. research/02 says Delhi's position is unconfirmed, and 16+2 is about half, not most.

Reading s.21: the advisory-SMC rule now covers 'minority schools and all other aided schools' (s.21(3)). Also added that specified-category schools need an SMC. Common traps and quick fact 7 updated to match.

Reading s.23 TET: filled in the ruling. Anjuman Ishaat-e-Taleem Trust judgment was Sept 2025; reviews were dismissed in May 2026; deadline is 31 Aug 2028 under Art 142; teachers with under 5 years of service left are exempt but cannot be promoted (research/05).
Reading Schedule: the 2022 amendment is dated 29 Sept 2022 and is described as PTR norms for special teachers (as listed in the DoSEL document).
Reading RPwD: Hindi term for benchmark disability 'निर्दिष्ट निःशक्तता' (means 'specified disability', a different term) → 'बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगता'.

Reading RPwD: 'UDID certificate (s.58)' → 'certificate of disability (s.58), now issued through the UDID system'. UDID is a scheme, not named in the Act. s.34 '1% each for four groups' → 'four categories of disability'.
Reading RPwD: removed the unverified NEP 2020 paragraph numbers (6.10–6.14). Now cited as Chapter 6, Equitable and Inclusive Education.
Reading JJ: the 2021 'serious offence' definition now also covers offences with a minimum below 7 years, not only those with no minimum.
Reading JJ: 'District Magistrate … registers … child care institutions' was wrong. Registration is by the State Government; the DM recommends it and has oversight powers.
Reading related laws: anti-bullying guidelines named precisely as NCPCR 'Preventing Bullying and Cyberbullying' guidelines 2024 (verified in research/02).
Remember #1: 'all three … in force 1 April 2010' → only Art 21A is stated as in force 1 April 2010. The commencement of Art 45 and Art 51A(k) could not be confirmed.

Verification limits: WebSearch was denied in this session. Checks were made against research/02-child-rights-law.md, research/05-current-affairs.md and the statute text. The 2026 items kept (Lucknow Public School, Anurudh, TET 31 Aug 2028) rest on research/05 tags ([OFF]/[NEWS]).
